chunks: Thereafter, He (God) settled Adam in a dwelling where He made his life pleasant and his stay safe,
So his enemy deceived him, envying him for his abiding in the dwelling and his companionship with the virtuous,
So he sold certainty for his doubt, and resolve for his weakness, and exchanged happiness for fear, and deception for regret.
Then God spread out for him in his repentance, and met him with the word of His mercy, and promised him return to his Paradise,
So He sent him down to the dwelling of trial and the procreation of progeny.
ai.seo_question: What is the narrative of Adam's fall and descent to Earth according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha elaborates on the theological narrative of Adam's fall, emphasizing the psychological mechanism of *ghurur* (deception through envy) and the exchange of certainty for doubt. It underscores the Shia scholarly view of Earth as *Dar al-Baliyyah* (abode of trial), framing human existence not merely as punishment but as a divinely ordained stage for spiritual testing and eventual return to Paradise through repentance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Thereafter, Allāh inhabited Adam (p.b.u.h.) in a house where He made his life pleasant and his stay safe, and He cautioned him of Iblis and his enmity.
Then his enemy (Iblis) envied his abiding in Paradise and his contacts with the virtuous.
So he changed his conviction into wavering and determination into weakness. He thus converted his happiness into fear and his prestige into shame.
Then Allāh offered to Adam (p.b.u.h.) the chance to repent, taught him words of His Mercy, promised him return to His Paradise
and sent him down to the place of trial and procreation of progeny.
